stem: In her science class in Jaipur, Meena learns that a human sperm cell and an egg cell each carry half the genetic material of a parent. Why does sexual reproduction not double the amount of genetic information in every new generation?

options.text: Each gamete carries half of a parent's genetic material, so joining two gametes restores the complete set of genetic instructions.
The parents give their complete genetic material to the offspring, so nothing is ever lost between generations.
Gametes from the two parents avoid mixing, so each offspring is an exact copy of only one parent.
Only one gamete takes part in fertilisation, so the genetic material stays the same.

teacher.key_rationale: Gametes carry half of each parent's genetic material; fertilisation joins the two half-sets to form a complete mix, preventing doubling each generation while still combining information from two parents. B is wrong because full material from each parent would double the instructions; C denies mixing of information from two parents; D contradicts fertilisation requiring two gametes.
